subtype: Approach: setting a fixed shutdown time [Action]
passage: So I decided the laptop closes at seven. Not "around seven". I set a reminder on my phone that just says "Close it", and I told my team the hours I would answer: nine to seven. I said it in the Monday stand-up, quickly, like pulling off a plaster. Nobody blinked. Our lead actually said thanks, because now there was something to plan around. It's funny. When the limit is only in my head, I bend it. When my team knows, it's harder to bend. The first week the reminder went off and I still wanted to finish one more email. I closed the laptop anyway. The email waited. I'm Jahnavi, by the way, and I'm still a bit surprised it worked.

qa.q: By what time does Jahnavi close the laptop?
What was Jahnavi feeling when the reminder went off with an email unfinished?
qa.a: Jahnavi felt tempted to keep going and a little uneasy about stopping, but closed the laptop anyway.

qa.q: What could help if a late request still comes from the lead?
qa.a: Jahnavi could point to the shared hours and offer a phone route for a true emergency, since the limit is now known to everyone.

qa.q: How might the team lead have seen the announcement?
qa.a: The lead likely appreciated it, since knowing Jahnavi's hours made planning easier.

grounding: Jahnavi sets a fixed shutdown time, adds a reminder and tells the team the hours to expect replies.

subtype: Approach: setting a fixed shutdown time [Action]
passage:
Indu sits across from me in the design pod, and for months she was the last light on. Last Monday something changed. At a quarter to seven her phone buzzed, she glanced at it, nodded and started saving files. At seven sharp the laptop lid came down.
That same afternoon she had posted in our team channel: "I'm reachable 9.30 to 7 on weekdays. Anything later I'll pick up the next morning. If something is truly on fire, call me." Our lead replied with a thumbs up.
On Wednesday a client note arrived at 7.20. Nobody pinged her; Rafi just flagged it for the morning. I can't say whether she finds it easy. She did look back at the dark screen once before leaving. But by Friday she was laughing at lunch again.
— Gurpreet

qa.q: What time did Indu close her laptop on Monday?
qa.a: At seven sharp the laptop lid came down, after her phone buzzed at a quarter to seven.

qa.q: What might Indu have felt when she looked back at the dark screen?
qa.a: She may have felt a flicker of unease or guilt about leaving on time, though the observer cannot be sure; by Friday she seemed more relaxed.

qa.q: What else could help Indu keep the seven o'clock limit on hard weeks?
qa.a: She could ask a teammate to nudge her at a quarter to seven, or agree with the lead on exactly what counts as something on fire.

qa.q: How does Gurpreet see the effect of Indu's message on the team?
qa.a: Gurpreet notices the team adjusting: when a late client note arrived, Rafi flagged it for morning instead of pinging Indu.

grounding: It shows a woman setting a fixed evening cut-off with a reminder and posting her reply hours to the team, and the team respecting those hours.

subtype: Approach: setting a fixed shutdown time [Action]
passage:
Monday, week one. Gopika's laptop is still open at 9.15 pm, a bowl of dal going cold beside it. Reena, her flatmate, asks if she has eaten. "After this one email," Gopika says, for the third time.
Thursday. Gopika sets a phone alarm labelled "Shut it: 7:00" and types a message to her team: "From next week I'll answer between 9 and 7. For anything urgent, please call." She hovers over send for a full minute, then presses it. Two people reply "noted".
Tuesday, week three. The alarm rings while she is mid-sentence in a document. She finishes the sentence, writes herself a note for tomorrow and closes the lid. A message arrives at 8. It isn't urgent; it waits. Gopika and Reena walk to the vegetable market before it shuts.

qa.q: What did Gopika label the phone alarm?
Why did Gopika hover over send for a full minute?
qa.a: She was nervous about how the team would react to fixed hours and perhaps worried it would look uncommitted; pressing send anyway shows her resolve.

qa.q: What small step helped Gopika close the lid mid-task, and what else could help?
qa.a: Writing herself a note for tomorrow let her stop without losing her place; on busy days she could also ask Reena to check in at seven.

qa.q: What is it like for Reena as the weeks change?
qa.a: Reena goes from watching her flatmate eat cold dal over email to having company for an evening walk to the market 😊

grounding: It shows the steps of fixing a closing time, setting a reminder and telling the team the reply hours, and how the clear expectation makes the limit easier to keep.
